fullAnalysis: Puzzle #678 resolves to "Words that come before phone" because each clue forms a familiar phone compound instead of pointing to a broad technology category.
Camera phone, smartphone, pay phone, touch-tone phone, and cellular phone all fit. Once you stop testing gadgets and instead test the shared word phone, the whole board locks quickly.

wordHints.Camera: Camera phone is a direct device phrase and one of the cleanest anchors.
wordHints.Smart: Smartphone confirms the same word family from consumer tech.
wordHints.Pay: Pay phone widens the pattern beyond modern devices.
wordHints.Touch-tone: Touch-tone phone keeps the same connector in an older telecom phrase.
wordHints.Cellular: Cellular phone verifies the category with a more formal term.

lessons.title: Tech clues often share a single connecting noun
lessons.body: Camera, smart, pay, and cellular all feel tech-adjacent but they don't share a gadget type. When clues point at a broad domain, test whether they all pair with the same everyday noun instead.

lessons.title: Old and new terms on the same board signal a word family
lessons.body: Pay phone is decades older than smartphone, yet both work here. Whenever old-fashioned and modern clues coexist, the connector is usually a shared word rather than a product era.

lessons.title: Verify with the least obvious clue last
lessons.body: Touch-tone is the most dated phrase in the set, but touch-tone phone is a perfectly standard term. Use your strongest anchors first, then confirm with the tricky clue — don't lead with the edge case.
